subject: Archive destruction sequencing & backup purge alignment
messages:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@medicorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@medicorp.com
Date: 2027-10-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on destruction sequencing and backup purge windows

Hi Soojin,

We're preparing for a compliance review (SOC2 + HIPAA scoped controls) and need to confirm several points in the DPA and our onboarding questionnaire:

- Exact sequencing for customer-initiated data deletion across primary storage, snapshots, and backups (we need a timeline to include in our audit evidence).
- Procedure and tooling for backup purges (how snapshots are tombstoned vs physically deleted).
- Log retention exceptions: what process we use to extend log retention for investigation, and how exceptions are recorded/approved.
- Subprocessor list and whether any subprocessor holds backups beyond Redwood's configured purge windows.

Can you provide a written plan and any artifacts you can attach (subprocessor matrix, proposed DPA redlines) by EOD Tuesday? We may need an attestation that deletions can be verified (S3 manifests or similar).

Thanks,
Megan Ortiz
Senior Manager, Compliance
Medicorp Health Systems

Attachment: request_form.pdf (stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@medicorp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-09T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on destruction sequencing and backup purge windows

Megan — thanks for the clear list. We can support the audit evidence you need and Ive started an internal coordination thread (cc'd Legal and Infra). Attached: current subprocessors matrix and our proposed DPA redlines (high level).

High-level proposal (for your review):
1) Deletion sequencing: mark objects as tombstoned in primary within 24 hours of request; snapshot markers applied immediately; physical retention windows applied to backups (default schedule below).
   - Tombstone (logical erase): 0-24 hours
   - Short-term snapshot retention (marked for purge): 30 days after tombstone
   - Physical removal from backups (final delete): 90 days after tombstone
2) Backup purge mechanics: weekly lifecycle job deletes objects flagged for removal; S3 manifests generated and stored for 180 days for verification.
3) Log retention exceptions: exceptions are approved via Change Control (legal approval + security ack); exception records live in our audit ledger and we can export for you.
4) Subprocessors: see matrix. Any subprocessor that stores backups is highlighted and we can require them to mirror our purge windows via contract clause.

Next steps: Kimberly, please review the DPA redlines for attestation language. Karthik, can you confirm the proposed manifest retention and provide a short playbook excerpt for how we prove deletion to a third party?

If this aligns, Megan, we'll formalize and share a DocuSign-ready amendment for signature.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Soojin — quick legal summary on the redlines:
- Add explicit "verification manifest" clause: Redwood will provide a signed manifest (hashes + S3 object keys + deletion timestamps) within 30 days of physical removal.
- Attestation: one-time attestation per purge event, included as a PDF delivered to the customer and stored on our evidence bucket for 365 days.
- Subprocessor carve: require subprocessors to provide the same manifest and attestation or flow the obligation back to Redwood.

Two asks for Infra: include a canary/rollback flag in the runbook so we can stop a weekly purge within a 48-hour window if a legal hold appears unexpectedly. Also, record every exception request in the legal approval ticket (Jira SUP-XXXXX).

I'll draft revised clause language and attach it to the DPA redlines.

-Kim
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on destruction sequencing and backup purge windows

Thanks — technical notes:
- Our deletion workflow already tombstones objects (logical delete) and maintains tombstone metadata in the primary index. Snapshots reference object versions; we mark snapshot entries as "to purge" at tombstone time.
- Weekly background job runs lifecycle transitions and issues S3 DeleteMarkers for objects older than the configured retention for that customer. We can emit an S3 inventory report (csv manifest) per purge job; we'll persist those manifests for 180 days by default.
- Canary/rollback: we can implement a 48-hour hold flag that pauses the weekly job per-customer. It requires a single infra toggle and an entry in the audit ledger.
- Edge case: cross-region replicas and cold archive (Glacier-like) — physical deletion from deep archive can take longer depending on vendor retention. We'll call this out in the manifest.

I attached a short playbook excerpt for evidence generation and the steps to generate the manifest (filenames, hash fields, deletion ts).

-karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@medicorp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on destruction sequencing and backup purge windows

Megan — consolidated plan below (apologies for the long note). Please review and reply with any dataset-specific exceptions.

Proposal (finalizable into a DPA amendment):
Phase A — Logical erase (Tombstone): within 24 hours of request. Customers can request immediate tombstone via API or via support/portal ticket.
Phase B — Snapshot marking: snapshot entries referencing deleted objects are marked for purge immediately; these are visible in the manifest as "marked_for_purge".
Phase C — Scheduled physical purge: weekly lifecycle job deletes objects marked for purge that have passed the snapshot window. Default schedule: 30-day snapshot hold, 90-day physical removal.
Evidence: after each weekly purge we will generate an S3 inventory CSV (object key, version id, sha256, tombstone_ts, deletion_ts) and produce a signed manifest PDF (legal attestation). Redwood will retain manifests for 365 days; raw CSV manifests retained for 180 days.
Exceptions: log-retention exception requests must be submitted to legal (kimberly.park) with justification; security (karthik.iyer) will approve technical feasibility. Exceptions will be recorded in Jira SUP-34567 and visible to customers on request.
Next steps:
- Action A (Infra): enable per-customer 48-hour purge pause flag (karthik).
- Action B (Legal): update DPA attestation clause and add subprocessor manifest requirement (kimberly).
- Action C (Sojourn): prepare DocuSign amendment and HubSpot entry (I will send this by EOD).

Im happy to walk through this in a 30-minute call if you prefer. If that plan works, well draft the amendment and send the DocuSign link for signature.

Regards,
Soojin

Thanks — the plan is helpful. A few clarifications: 
1) For certain PHI datasets we cannot accept a 90-day physical removal window; would Redwood consider 45 days for scoped datasets?
2) For attestation we need the manifest plus an S3 inventory snapshot (or equivalent vendor log) retained for 365 days — can you confirm the CSV retention will be extended to 365 days for those scoped datasets?
3) Well want the ability to trigger an accelerated purge per dataset with a documented change control path and a signature from our security lead.

If you can confirm answers to (1)-(3) I think we can move to the amendment. Were happy to take the call on Tuesday morning.

Best,
Megan
